programme.desc: The actor explores some of the most important archaeological finds in Ireland's history, revealing how many have been used as an important tool for nation-building on both sides of the border. Speaking to world-renowned experts, he unravels a forgotten time period, when a team of Americans from Harvard University, a Nazi archaeologist from Austria, and a Welsh geography professor dug up ancient sites across the country. programme.title: Kamikaze: An Untold History
programme.desc: On the Pacific front, towards the end of the Second World War, Japan's imperial armed forces launched kamikaze attacks - suicide missions by aircraft laden with bombs. Close to 4,000 Japanese airmen died, and nearly 7,000 Allied military personnel were killed, and thousands more were injured by the attacks. How could this happen? Utilising 15 years' worth of extensive interviews with US and Japanese veterans, Takayuki Oshima's film delves into the mechanism of how a crazed madness swept through an entire nation

programme.title: The Sky at Night

programme.title: The Wildest Weather in the Universe: Horizon

programme.title: Beautiful Equations

programme.desc: Tink becomes consumed with a golden seat, but the King is after it also, after being told by Bgais-shd that it holds great powers

programme.title: Fuine (Home Baking)
programme.desc: Gregor MacLeod makes lemon custard-filled Genovese biscuits from Sicily with soft buttery pastry. Taking inspiration from Greece, he also reveals a quick recipe for light and fluffy giant pitta breads

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: With Andrew Ditton, whose love of Gaelic inspired a move to Uist, and Calum Maclean visits Airth in Stirlingshire where he discovers a fruity architectural surprise

programme.title: An L (News)
programme.desc: Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts a new fun quiz show where Rona and Miri; and Seoras and Sean go head-to-head to win a cash prize. Standing in the way of victory are the Pretenders

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara (Mermaid Tales)
programme.desc: Kate MacLeod, aka The Hebridean Mermaid, explores the hidden gems of the Hebrides, meeting tradition bearers with remarkable stories about the places she loves to visit the most, above and below the water. In this episode she comes across an interesting sea creature, known as a sunfish, which is native to tropical waters, but is likely to have been carried to the islands by the Gulf Stream. Swimming on its side, the sun heats its body and it feeds on jellyfish. She also journeys to Taransay, home of some of the most stunning and unique beaches in the Outer Hebrides. Once a thriving community, the island had three villages, but is now home to deer, seabirds and cattle.

programme.title: Faodail: Found
programme.desc: The Faodail Film Archive celebrates lost indigenous film collections from the 1930s to the 1980s in the Outer Hebrides, preserving the archive for future generations. The Cinema Sgre Continuing mobile cinema van travels the islands, showcasing footage to local communities, making them accessible globally online, and adding rich new narratives relevant to the Gidhealtachd for contemporary audiences

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions: Dlth an Dimh
programme.desc: Julie Fowlis and Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh present highlights from two decades of the music show, featuring Aoife O'Donovan, Dirk Powell and Allison Moorer

programme.title: An t-Eilean (The Island)
programme.desc: A young family liaison officer is assigned to investigate the brutal murder of Lady Mary Maclean, wife of local tycoon Sir Douglas, at a remote island mansion. The investigation unravels on the island of Harris, from where the officer mysteriously fled 10 years previously. The evidence points towards the murder being committed by a violent intruder during a botched burglary. However, when Sir Douglas' account of the night fails to match the evidence, Kat starts to believe that the motive for the killing may lead straight back to the family. Mystery, starring Sorcha Groundsell and Iain Macrae. In Gaelic and English

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Abigail MacIver takes the audience through her favourite brunch recipes. She shares an idea for an unusual treat - a Dutch baby

programme.title: Seid a' Chidsin - The Kitchen Coves
programme.desc: The lads are inspired to cook Japanese dishes. Roddy creates a Wagyu Sukiyaki and a Salmon Teriyaki accompanied by Pak Choi and noodles. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: World's Ultimate Adventures
programme.desc: Chef and content creator Julie Lin is on a Turkish adventure - combining her passion for food with history. Travelling through the south east, known as the gastronomic heart, she first stops in the city of Gazianetep - world famous for its baklava. Julie uncovers what makes this delicacy and the locally grown pistachios inside it so special. Heading further east, she visits the Neolithic site of Karahan Tepe, a discovery so significant that it is reshaping our understanding of human history. Guided by the archaeological team, Julie explores their latest finds, including what may be the world's oldest kitchen. Her journey ends in ?anl?urfa, cooking with a family keeping traditional recipes alive, discovering the city's signature smoked pepper, and finishing her trip with a vibrant cultural, night-time celebration and an unusual raw-meat dish.

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: Notts County v Leicester City (Kick-off 12.00pm). Coverage of the League One match at Meadow Lane. It has been a turbulent few years for Leicester, who have endured financial difficulties and been relegated in each of the last two seasons. In contrast, the Magpies were playing non-league football three seasons ago, but have been promoted twice since then to reach the third tier for the first time since the 2014/15 campaign

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: York City v Bristol Rovers (Kick-off 3.00pm). Coverage of both teams' opening League Two match of the season, held at LNER Community Stadium. York won the National League last term to secure a place in the Football League since they were relegated in the 2015/16 season, but their title-winning manager Stuart Maynard departed during the summer and was replaced by Scott Lindsey. Their opponents will be looking to improve on last season's 14th-place finish and push for promotion

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: Sheffield United v Birmingham City (kick-off 5.30pm). Coverage of both teams' opening match of the Championship season, held at Bramall Lane. United claimed a 3-0 win in last season's corresponding fixture thanks to goals by Tyler Bindon, Gustavo Hamer and Patrick Bamford, but Birmingham were reduced to 10 men in the 18th minute due to Tommy Doyle's red card when the score was 1-0

programme.title: European Athletics Championships: Birmingham 2026
programme.desc: Jeanette Kwakye presents coverage of the opening session on day two from Alexander Stadium. Marcell Jacobs of Italy begins his bid for a third consecutive European 100m title in the heats. The women's 800m also gets under way and is one of the most eagerly anticipated events this time around, with Team GB's reigning champion Keely Hodgkinson expected to face stiff competition from the likes of Femke Broeders-Bol and Audrey Werro. The women's 400m hurdles semi-finals also take place, with reigning champion Bol not defending her title, leaving Emma Zapletalova as the pre-event favourite. With analysis from Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, and commentary by Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe

programme.desc: Gabby Logan presents coverage of the evening session on day six from Alexander Stadium in Birmingham, including the men's and women's 4x100m finals. It will also be hoped that Katarina Johnson Thompson can win a medal in the heptathlon, which concludes with the 800m, and Jake Wightman will be quietly confident in the 1500m, knowing that mile world record holder and Commonwealth title winner Josh Kerr is not taking part in these championships. A busy evening also sees medals awarded in the women's high jump and 400m, and the men's javelin, triple jump and 10,000m. With analysis from Jessica Ennis-Hill, Jenny Meadows and Greg Rutherford, and commentary by Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe
